skills.name: audience-research
skills.description: Mine where your audience actually talks (reviews, Reddit, YouTube comments, communities) and produce two brand files, audience.md (segments, awareness, jobs-to-be-done, watering holes) and voc.md (verbatim pain/desire/objection language with sources). Use it before positioning or copy work, when launching into a new market, or when copy keeps missing because nobody knows how customers actually describe the problem.

skills.name: brand-voice
skills.description: Extracts or builds a falsifiable brand voice profile, backed by verbatim evidence from the brand's real content, that every other content skill reads, so output sounds like the brand instead of a model. Use when starting a project, when copy sounds generic or AI-written, when output must match a specific person or brand, or to check recently published content for voice drift.

skills.name: content-atomizer
skills.description: Turns one piece of finished content (blog post, newsletter, podcast, video) into platform-native social assets for the 2-3 platforms the brand actually operates, with depth on a few platforms instead of rephrased spray across eight. Use when source content exists and needs distribution, when a post's comments need ranked reply drafts, or when a week of posts should be planned from one source.

skills.name: creative
skills.description: AI creative production engine for product photos, product video, social graphics, talking heads, ad creative, and video ads cut from real or generated footage in code and rendered to MP4 for free, through one tiered pipeline with a vision-QA loop that looks at every asset before you see it. Ad creative is built from 336 live Meta ads we viewed (21 formats with real examples, a hook bank, a script that pulls competitors' live ads from the Meta Ad Library, a batch plan that mixes long-running stills with fresh UGC, and a visual check every ad must pass). Use whenever visual assets or ad creative need to be made, edited, planned, or batch-produced for a brand or campaign.

skills.name: direct-response-copy
skills.description: Write copy that converts (landing pages, sales pages, emails, ads, headlines, CTAs) in the customer's own words, matched to the ad or email that sends the traffic. A claim gate keeps every shipped line to verified facts (stronger ideas go on a To make this true list), and a private score-and-rewrite loop lifts the draft. Includes local-service patterns for copy that makes the phone ring. Approved page copy hands off to /landing-page to build. Use when someone needs to sell in writing, wants copy scored, or has ads that get clicks but no sales or calls.

skills.name: keyword-research
skills.description: Maps what people search for and ask about a business as a topic map rather than a 5,000-row keyword list, using free autocomplete and Search Console first, covering both Google searches and the questions people put to AI assistants, going deep only on the topics worth acting on, and ending in ready-to-write briefs. Use when planning content, choosing what to write about, finding content gaps, or building an SEO and AI-search plan, for an online business or a local one.

skills.name: landing-page
skills.description: Turn an offer into a shipped landing page with section architecture chosen by offer type and awareness level, a first screen that repeats the ad's promise word for word, a deployable build (single-file HTML or Next.js) with A/B variant routes, and an optional deploy; includes a teardown mode that scores any live page section-by-section into a prioritized rewrite plan (the conversion-audit capability), and a local section for service businesses (call-first page vs quote form vs booking, plus a phone first-screen checklist). Use when the user wants a page built, has approved copy that needs to become a working page, has ads that get clicks but no sign-ups or calls, or has a live page that isn't converting.

skills.name: lead-magnet
skills.description: Generate lead magnet concepts grounded in live competitor research, then BUILD the chosen one, including working interactive apps (quiz, calculator, instant quote, AI-graded audit) with a capture gate, as well as written guides and checklists. Covers info products, SaaS, agencies and local service businesses (price calculators, repair-or-replace checkers, seasonal checklists, financing estimates), plus an automated free-report Zap. Use when someone wants more leads or subscribers, needs top-of-funnel ideas, or asks what to give away for free.

skills.name: long-form-article
skills.description: Plans, researches and drafts one long guide (3,000 to 5,000 words) for an X Article, a LinkedIn article, a blog or a newsletter, with a point a reader could repeat, named and dated sources, a proven structure from the size of the gap to "start this week", copyable prompts or steps, an honest "what breaks", and optional images. Use when you want a long-form piece, a playbook, a masterplan or a definitive guide that becomes the go-to resource on a topic.

skills.name: newsletter
skills.description: Write publication-ready newsletter editions, roundup, deep-dive, personal essay, curated links, news briefing, or hybrid, in the brand's voice, sourced from live pages, and informed by the list's own click data when an ESP key exists. Use it to draft an edition, pick a format, or answer newsletter strategy questions (platform, growth, monetization).

skills.name: positioning-angles
skills.description: Find the angle and the offer that make something sell. Researches what competitors say and pay to say, mines their bad reviews for the fears nobody answers, reads how jaded the market is, then writes 3-5 angles with one starred. Shipped lines use only verified facts, and a stronger idea the business can't back yet goes on a To make this true list with what it would take. Has a local-service mode (job types, map-pack competitors, trade guarantees). Use when launching a product or service, building an offer or lead magnet, before writing a page, or when marketing isn't converting.

skills.name: programmatic-seo
skills.description: Validate, build, and ship a programmatic SEO library (one template × one dataset → 50-500 pages that each earn their existence with unique data). Use when a keyword pattern repeats across a modifier set (x for [industry], [city] x, x vs y, x alternatives, x integrations) and pages should be generated from data instead of written one at a time. A local service business that wants town or service-area pages uses /service-area-pages instead.

skills.name: seo-content
skills.description: Write publication-ready articles that earn classic rankings AND AI-surface citations (AI Overviews, ChatGPT search, Perplexity) while reading like a human expert wrote them. Use when turning a keyword or content brief into an actual piece. It scrapes the live SERP with parallel agents, captures who the AI surfaces cite and why, drafts in your voice, humanizes, optimizes on two tracks (on-page + GEO), and ships valid 2026 schema. Refresh mode diffs both the SERP and the AI-citation set against your published article.

skills.name: service-area-pages
skills.description: Writes town and service-area pages for a local business that each say something true and specific about that town, folds the towns that can't into one honest areas-we-serve page, and checks the set for duplicates before anything ships. Use when a plumber, roofer, HVAC company or other service-area business needs city pages, wants to fix town pages that are all the same, or has a local SEO plan that calls for them.

skills.name: site-audit
skills.description: Crawls a website the way Google and the AI crawlers see it and returns a short, ranked fix list in plain words. It covers pages blocked from Google, noindex and canonical mistakes, AI crawlers blocked in robots.txt or at the CDN, sitemap health, broken links, duplicate and thin pages, Core Web Vitals from Google's free PageSpeed API, and the content signals that make a page worth citing. Use for a technical SEO audit, when pages aren't showing up on Google, to check whether AI crawlers can reach the site, or to re-check a site after fixes and see what changed.

skills.name: social-content
skills.description: Writes original X and LinkedIn posts from the user's own best posts and real numbers, not generic hooks. Builds a per-user pattern library (what wins in their niche plus their own canon), then writes every post finished from the facts in hand (at most one fact flagged to verify), scores it privately against a calibrated rubric, checks it for the tells that make posts sound written by AI, and runs quote-post, reply and weekly modes. When the user sells a service, adds a launch arc, a low-friction offer and a daily engagement-to-DM routine tied to the goal. Use for writing original social posts; to repurpose existing long-form content use /content-atomizer.
